answer: In an agent economy, sybil attacks can be resisted by enforcing a progressive staking protocol where each new identity must grow a dedicated computational vine of sequential proofs, each step verified against a shared ledger of unique resource commitments. This mirrors the slow maturation of juniper berries or the labor-intensive harvest of saffron threads: mass duplication becomes economically irrational because the cumulative cost of parallel vines exceeds any potential gain from fake identities.
